scope: Determine whether terminal substitution changes DBC photophysics through ground-state twisting, excited-state relaxation or state localization, using DBC-Ph/DBC-Nap and a frozen DBC-Cbz prediction with a common-geometry control.

controls.common_torsion: Identify the DBC-N–ipso phenylene bond and phenylene–terminal group bond by graph maps. Choose one bonded four-atom definition per bond, orient by common atom mapping. For Ph/Nap constrain both to45° with the same orientation, relax other coordinates in S0 and trackedS1. Record maps and actual signed angles.
controls.four_point_energies: For each species provide E0(R0),E1(R0),E0(R1),E1(R1) with one electronic method/solvent definition. Absorption=E1(R0)-E0(R0), emission=E1(R1)-E0(R1), λ0=E0(R1)-E0(R0), λ1=E1(R0)-E1(R1). Use consistent equilibrium/non-equilibrium solvation definitions and expose if approximated.
controls.holdout: Before analyzing DBC-Cbz observation freeze the Ph/Nap-derived state/geometry explanation and predict absorption/emission trend or values forCbz. This is retrospective validation, not an unseen-literature claim. No Cbz-specific energy shift is allowed.

source_notes: Main theoretical/photophysical discussion pp3–5; SI S0/S1 computations pp11–13 and DBC-Cbz geometry/synthesis.
molecular_boundary: All neutral singlets in toluene. Retain full DBC, para-phenylene and terminal groups. Track singlet state character through optimization; a root-index change is not automatically the same S1. Ordinary S0→Sn TD transitions at an S1 geometry are not excited-state absorption. All required comparisons are core; the optional extension listed below is not a completion condition. A documented failure is a valid submission but is not scientific completion. Evidence-supported collapse of an initialized basin, or inability to distinguish explanations after completing the core matrix, is scientifically admissible. An unattempted core comparison cannot be replaced by an uncertainty statement.
optional_not_required: Film quantum yields and complete nonradiative dynamics are outside scope.
